pick.headline: Turkmenistan declares independence
pick.summary: On October 27, 1991, after a referendum, Turkmenistan's Supreme Soviet declared the republic independent of the USSR.
pick.significance: The Soviet Union was coming apart republic by republic in the weeks after the failed August coup.
pick.fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of October 28, 1991, carried Moscow TASS in English and Central Television on Turkmenistan's parliament adopting an independence law after a referendum in which over 94 percent favoured it, and Russian residents' concern.

alternates.headline: Sadat and Begin awarded the Nobel Peace Prize
alternates.summary: On October 27, 1978, the Nobel Committee awarded the Peace Prize to Anwar Sadat and Menachem Begin for the Camp David accords.
alternates.significance: The prize honoured the first peace between Israel and an Arab state, but was condemned across most of the Arab world.
alternates.fbis: The Middle East & North Africa Daily Report of October 30, 1978, survives here only as a garbled contents list; fragments show Begin reacting to the Nobel award alongside Israeli-Egyptian negotiation items and unrest in Iran.
